correctness.rationale: The prime and \(n=1\) evaluations are exact. Squarefree composites split by Möbius sign: odd support removes the parameter and the product difference is strictly larger than two, while even support gives a uniform positive margin surviving all \(t>-2\). If a prime cube divides \(n\), both the inverse divisor term and Möbius term vanish and positivity is immediate. In the cube-free nonsquarefree case \(n=ab^2\), the only delicate odd-\(\mu(a)\) branch reduces to proving \(J_k(a)J_k(b)>\sigma_k(a)\); the Euler-product bound \(\sigma_k(a)/J_k(a)<\zeta(k)^2/\zeta(2k)\le5/2<3\le J_k(b)\) proves this strictly. Fresh exact arithmetic through \(n=2000\), \(2\le k\le5\), and several rational \(t>-2\) reproduced prime-only zeros.
correctness.risk: The theorem is a structural characterization, not an efficient primality test because direct evaluation typically presupposes factorization.

However, in the crucial cube-free nonsquarefree case that proof uses only divisibility/integrality to exclude one target value; it does not establish the strict sign needed to interpolate an arbitrary real coefficient. value.rationale: The result identifies the maximal coefficient-stability region joining two published prime characterizations and locates its exact first obstruction. The required strict sign lemma clarifies which part of the original factorization proof is robust under perturbation, making this more than a cosmetic interpolation.
value.risk: It does not improve computational primality testing.

final_claim: For every integer \(k\ge2\), the equation \(\sigma_k^{(-1)}(n)+J_k(n)+2+t(\mu(n)+1)=0\) detects exactly the primes for every real \(t>-2\), and \((-2,\infty)\) is the maximal open interval containing the published cases \(t=0\) and \(t=1\), because \(t=-2\) also annihilates \(n=1\).
limitations: Structural criterion rather than an efficient algorithm.
